lesson.title: ਪੰਜਾਬ ਬਾਰੇ ਇੱਕ ਦਲੀਲ (A Persuasive Piece About Punjab)
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: ਹੁਣ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਵਰਤਣ ਦੀ ਵਾਰੀ! (Now it's time to use everything!) Today, real persuasive writing in Punjabi.

New words for persuasion: ਸੋਹਣਾ (sohna, beautiful), ਦੇਖਣਾ (dekhna, to see/visit), and ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ (zaroori, important). Using this week's vocabulary (ਦਰਿਆ, ਖੇਤ, ਖੇਤੀਬਾੜੀ, ਸ਼ਹਿਰ, ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ), write a short persuasive piece (3-4 sentences) arguing why someone should visit or learn about Punjab. Make a real claim (ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇਖਣਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਹੈ — 'visiting Punjab is important'), then give at least two specific reasons using this week's geography vocabulary.
ਸ਼ਾਬਾਸ਼! (Well done!) You just wrote a real persuasive piece in Punjabi, using genuine geography vocabulary as your evidence.

objectives: Learn 3 new persuasive vocabulary words: ਸੋਹਣਾ, ਦੇਖਣਾ, ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ
Write a short persuasive piece using a claim and reasons drawn from this week's geography vocabulary
materialsNeeded: This week's earlier worksheets for vocabulary reference
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's geography vocabulary (rivers, farmland, Amritsar).
2. Introduce today's 3 persuasive words.
3. Model the claim sentence, then have the child add 2 reasons using known vocabulary.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the claim sentence and have the child focus only on writing the 2 supporting reasons
Ready for more: challenge them to add a persuasive concluding sentence beyond the claim and reasons
All Gurmukhi words/phrases used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary — check the piece includes a real claim and at least 2 specific reasons using this week's vocabulary (rivers, farmland, or Amritsar), not vague generalities.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'persuasive writing' description, using this week's real geography vocabulary as genuine supporting evidence rather than an isolated grammar exercise.
